resources.title: Compare two settlement samples
paragraphs_in_document_order: Compare two settlement samples
Tuesday 8 December 2026 | P2 | 40 minutes | Year A

Teach one 40-minute comparison lesson to the LAUNCH pair. Use fictional Place A, an inland settlement, and fictional Place B, a coastal settlement. Each has a matched twenty-plot sample. Pupils use prepared source cards, a data graph and schematic maps, then retain an individual evidence-based comparison.
Scheme and success

Weekly objective, LAUNCH Weekly - Autumn!C58: Compare a contrasting place (online resources). Theme: Identity & Belonging. Unit, LAUNCH - Autumn!D11, generic wording: Geography: place, settlement & urbanisation. Assessment, J11: F: map/GIS skills checks.  S: fieldwork enquiry write-up (Dec).
I can compare the same features with exact numbers and a source. I can distinguish a description from a possible explanation. I can explain a limitation and what would need checking.

Evidence HUM-LAUNCH-A2-W06-E1: one own comparison note with at least one similarity and one contrast across two matched features, plot counts, source codes, possible explanation and limitation. Retain actual help, adult reply, NS and own response. Actual outcomes and banking remain blank.
Before teaching

Prepare S1–S3, one chosen route page, word mat, graph/maps and evidence form. Offer White or Pink paper by preference. Both learners can read quietly, point, write, type or direct a scribe. No cold calling or required reading aloud. Bring earlier Weeks 4–5 fieldwork only as an approved anonymous copy; check sampling method, units, categories and sample sizes before any authentic comparison. Otherwise use the labelled fictional baseline. Keep original fieldwork intact and private.
Where this leads

A survey or planning assistant checks the source, unit and method before comparing places. They report a useful pattern while keeping the sample’s limits clear. A confident explanation needs evidence, not an attractive graph alone.
Access and adult support

Offer a reduced-source route, one feature at a time, a category key, quiet processing time, sentence frames or the usual aid. Analyst and Checker roles swap; neither pupil is a permanent helper. Keep actual reading, calculation and scribing support separate from independent work. Geography comparison does not rank communities or people.
Compare two settlement samples continued
Tuesday 8 December 2026 | P2 | 40 minutes | Year A
Forty minute teaching sequence
Slide
Min
Teacher and support action
Introduce the exact weekly objective. Explain that online resources are supplied as internal cards; no live search or external links are used.
Private arrival check and usual regulation choice. No learner must read aloud or answer publicly.
Retrieve a map key and model grid reference, settlement features, sampling units and spreadsheet/graph checks from Weeks 1–5 without inventing learner results.
Agree success: same-feature comparisons, exact plot counts and sources, one possible explanation and a limitation.
Model residential plots: A12, B6, difference6. Link the S2 table to the graph. Label the example fictional and separate description from cause.
Use the editable comparison table and S1–S3. Find the workshop similarity and test the private hinge: count evidence does not prove a coastal cause.
Seven minutes: Analyst chooses one feature, Checker verifies source, category, count and unit. Swap after the first comparison. Keep one similarity and one contrast.

Ten minutes: each learner writes, types, points or directs an exact scribe for their own note. Include numbers/source, possible explanation and limit; hear adult reply and one NS, then retain own response.
Check evidence boundaries: twenty sampled plots, one route per place, one day, no whole-place or cause claim. Actual help and any remaining gap stay visible.
Private exit: one checked comparison and the limitation it needs. Keep preparation notes for the later fieldwork write-up; do not treat the model as authentic fieldwork.
Use vocabulary throughout, privately or with an aid. Offer reduced-source load, frame, processing time and optional exact scribing.

Hidden adult brief. Prompt ladder: point to the place/instruction; short question; rephrase; scaffold/choice; model the first step only, then return the task. No cold calling or required reading aloud.
Quiet hinge and reteach

Ask privately or offer a written choice: “S2 shows six open-space plots in B and two in A. Does that prove the coast caused the difference?” No. This is a description of two samples. Other route areas or coding choices might affect it. If a learner infers cause, return to S1 method and ask what new evidence could test that explanation.
Paired and individual practice

Use seven minutes for a shared check, then ten for each learner’s own response. Analyst selects a same-category comparison; Checker checks both counts, units and source, then swap. Each learner retains an individual final note. A partner’s completed answer is not evidence for both.
Compare two settlement samples continued
Tuesday 8 December 2026 | P2 | 40 minutes | Year A
Routes and visible finish

Supported: choose two features with a frame; keep one similarity, one contrast, numbers and a limit. Independent: explain those comparisons with sources, a possible reason and a limit; add another contrast if useful. Aspire: check proportions, a second contrast or alternative explanation and propose a stronger sample. All routes finish with an individual note and an honest next check.
Evidence boundaries

S1–S3 and the data set are fictional models. Twenty plots on one route per place on one day are snapshots. Plot counts are not population or land area. The schematic map is not a real survey map or a metric distance plan. Matching categories and sample sizes help comparison but do not establish representativeness or causation. Use an actual local sample only if its anonymity and comparability have been checked; never relabel this model as the pupil’s fieldwork.
Communication and feedback

Offer an authentic comparison explanation to the Communication portfolio. Keep the learner’s own idea, adult audience reply, one NS and own-colour or supported response before recording R. E records only actual evidence banking. VF verbal feedback, WS support, I independent, NS next step, // self-edit and ? read this back may be used privately; no reading aloud is required. Record actual help and any learner request or change.
Actual delivery date __________  Help actually used __________Adult reply/NS __________  Own response __________Unfinished check __________  Actual banking __________
Next sequence step

Week 7, Tuesday 15 December 2026, is the assessing fieldwork enquiry write-up from actual Weeks 4–5 collection, spreadsheet and graph work. Today prepares comparison notes only. Keep the real fieldwork, source references and method limitations ready. Missing real data stays a gap; model practice does not establish completed fieldwork or an award.

resources.title: Staff answers and evidence limits
paragraphs_in_document_order: Staff answers and evidence limits
Tuesday 8 December 2026 | P2 | 40 minutes | Year A
The intended comparison

Source objective: Compare a contrasting place (online resources). Prepared internal cards supply this session's comparison. Fictional Place A is the baseline. Retrieve grid references, digital mapping, settlement features, sampling and spreadsheet graphs as prior skills; invent no earlier learner results.
Matched model answers

S2 shows residential plots: A 12, B 6. The contrast is six plots, or 60% versus 30% of equal twenty-plot samples. The optional difference is thirty percentage points. Workshops are two plots in each sample, or 10% each: a similarity. Services are A 4 and B 6; open space A 2 and B 6. Both totals are twenty. Accept other accurate matched comparisons, but require one similarity and one contrast across two features.
A defensible final note

Example only: S2 shows two workshop plots in each sample. A has twelve residential plots and B six, a difference of six. Routes may cross different settlement areas. S1 describes one short route per place on one day, so more routes are needed before describing the whole place. This model is not a pupil outcome.
An unjustified claim

Reject: The coast caused more open space, so Place B is better. S2 shows a count difference but provides no causal test or basis for ranking places. Ask which part is description, which is an explanation and what evidence would test it. There is no single correct settlement preference.
Staff answers and evidence limits continued
Tuesday 8 December 2026 | P2 | 40 minutes | Year A
Evidence and access

Swap Analyst and Checker roles after the first comparison. Keep each learner's final response and actual help. Offer pointing, writing, quiet collaboration, exact scribing or the usual aid. No cold calling or forced reading aloud. A partner's answer cannot prove both understand.
Correct the likely errors

If features are mismatched, return to the category key and compare the same row. If totals differ, do not compare raw counts as though samples were equal; check proportions and method first. If thirty percentage points becomes thirty per cent, use 60% minus 30% and label the unit. If plot counts become population or area, return to S1's sampling unit.
Authentic data and privacy

Use earlier fieldwork only from an approved nameless copy with compatible categories, sample sizes and method checked. Retain real gaps and limitations. If matching is not possible, use the fictional cards and label the work MODEL. Keep names, locations and identifying details separately. Never relabel model data as local fieldwork.
The boundary before next week

Week 6 prepares notes. The later fieldwork enquiry write-up uses actual fieldwork; it is not produced or claimed complete here. Retain sources, explanations and checks. Record an adult reply, next-step prompt and own response only when they happen. Banking and qualification decisions stay separate; any award wording stays [AWARD] or [QUAL].

Card 1 check the match

Look at S1 and S2. What is counted? Plots. How many? Twenty on each route. Do both use R, S, W and O? Yes. What is still limited? One route in each fictional place on one day. Point to the matching category before comparing it.
Card 2 find a similarity
Look for a category with the same count. Check both values in S2. Frame: Both sampled routes have __ __ plots. I checked source __. Keep the category and the unit; do not change plots into people.
Card 3 find a contrast

Choose a different category and compare the same feature in both places. Frame: Place A's route has __ __ plots. Place B's route has __. The difference is __ plots. The source is __. A contrast can go in either direction.
Our partner roles

Analyst: choose the feature and make the comparison. Checker: match the code, numbers, unit and source. Swap after the first comparison. You may point, write or speak quietly. You do not have to read aloud. No cold calling. Each learner makes their own final note.

White paper version | Read quietly. Point, write, type or use a scribe. No reading aloud is required.
Card 4 explain with care

A description tells what the numbers show. An explanation suggests why. Frame: One possible explanation is __. We would need __ to check this. The routes might pass different parts of the settlements. The counts do not prove that coastal location caused the difference.
Card 5 keep a limit

Choose a real limit from S1 or S3. Frame: This is only __, so we cannot claim __. A next check could be __. Think about more routes, another day or how mixed-use plots receive one primary code. Keep the model separate from real fieldwork.

Use the same denominator: twenty plots. Residential is 12 out of 20, or 60%, in A; 6 out of 20, or 30%, in B. The difference is thirty percentage points. Workshops are 10% in both. This step extends the comparison; it does not replace an accurate count sentence.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Words for comparing settlement samples
Tuesday 8 December 2026 | P2 | 40 minutes | Year A
White paper version | Read quietly. Point, write, type or use a scribe. No reading aloud is required.
Evidence words

Sample: a small set chosen to study.Plot: one unit of land recorded in this model.Primary code: the one main use recorded for a plot.Residential: mainly used for homes.Services: uses that serve people.Workshop: a place for making or repairing.Open space: an area recorded as open land.
Comparison words

Similarity: a feature that is alike.Contrast: a difference in the same feature.Proportion: a part compared with its whole.Percentage point: the unit for subtracting one percentage from another.Description: what the evidence shows.Tentative explanation: a possible reason that needs checking.Limitation: something the evidence cannot establish.Snapshot: a record of a limited time and sample.
Map and source words

Inland: away from the coast.Coastal: next to the coast.Schematic: a simplified display, not an exact real map.Source code: a label showing where a claim came from.Representative: able to reflect a wider group fairly. One short route is not enough to assume this.
Words for my final note

Both samples have __. A has __ and B has __. Source __ shows __. One possible reason is __. The evidence is limited because __. We need __ to check it.FINISH: one similarity and one contrast, with numbers, sources and a limit. Point, write or speak quietly; use your usual aid. No forced reading aloud or cold calling.

I have two features, a similarity and a contrast.
My explanation is tentative and my limit is clear.
GREEN: I can show the source for my claim.
AMBER: I need to add or check evidence.
RED: I need help with one step.
My own correction or next check is __.

slides.notes:
HUM-LAUNCH-A2-W06 · Year A · Tuesday 8 December 2026 · P2
Evidence check before hand-in: 3 minutes.
Teacher: Check each individual response for two matched features, one similarity and one contrast with evidence, a tentative explanation and a limit. Readiness colours also have explicit words, and learners may point or respond privately. Keep the one-route, one-day sampling limit and distinguish a sample pattern from the whole place. Record actual evidence status only after review.
Weekly objective: Compare a contrasting place (online resources).

HUM-LAUNCH-A2-W06 · Year A · Tuesday 8 December 2026 · P2
Exit ticket: 2 minutes.
Teacher: Hear or collect one individual exit line from each learner without cold calling. An unfinished question can stay open. Next week, Tuesday 15 December 2026, is the assessing write-up of actual fieldwork. Today’s fictional comparison, graph and schematic map must never be relabelled as the learner’s actual fieldwork findings.

slides.notes:
HUM-LAUNCH-A2-W06 · Year A · Tuesday 8 December 2026 · P2
Key vocabulary mat: 0 minutes.
Teacher: Use this word mat throughout. Explain residential as plots mainly for homes, services as plots mainly providing a service, workshops as plots mainly for making or repairing, and open space as plots mainly open. The same primary-code rule applies in both samples. Offer reading support and a speaking or writing frame without replacing the learner’s own comparison.

shape_text.name: staff-main
shape_text.text:
One pair: Analyst and Checker, then swap.
Keep an individual response from each learner.
Use quiet reading, pointing, writing or scribing.
Do not turn the model into actual fieldwork.
R: adult reply, NS and own response.
E: record only actual evidence banking.

shape_text.name: cold-call-detail
shape_text.text:
No cold calling or required reading aloud.
1. Which source supports this comparison?
2. What can the sample not tell us?
3. What other cause or check is possible?

slides.notes:
HUM-LAUNCH-A2-W06 · Year A · Tuesday 8 December 2026 · P2
TA and staff brief: 0 minutes.
Teacher: Hidden adult brief, not part of the displayed teaching sequence. Prompt ladder: point to the place or instruction; ask a short question; rephrase; provide a scaffold or choice; model the first step only, then return the task. No cold calling or required reading aloud. Preserve each learner’s own work and actual support. R requires an actual adult audience reply, one NS and the learner’s own-colour or supported response. E records actual banking only. Qualification mapping stays a separate staff check; no unit or award is inferred.
